gap: No result ChatGPT got states the 15-inch MacBook Air's own lab-measured screen and battery figures (Notebookcheck: 546 cd/m² peak, 224 PPI, 66.5 Wh, 16 h 28 min Wi-Fi at 150 cd/m²) beside the extenders' figures, which shows every pick is dimmer and coarser than the Air's panel and that a bus-powered Duex Float 2 Pro (7.5 W per Macworld) would cut that runtime to roughly 5.8 hours by arithmetic.
standout_why: Compared against Macworld's roundup (cited), thisUSB (cited), Dealectric's best-laptop-screen-extender and under-300 pages (cited), and Macworld's Duex Float 2 Pro review. Macworld's roundup gives spec-list figures with no stated measurement method and never mentions the MacBook Air. thisUSB says it does not test and uses maker sheets only, with no Mobile Pixels product. Our general page already carries Macworld's 7.5 W / 80% figure and a 7.2-hour arithmetic, so the power-draw half is partly covered. None gives a measured baseline for the Air 15 itself, a PPI comparison, or the weight added as a share of the Air's weight. Weak point: I found no named lab measurement of the Duex Max DS, Duex Float 2 Pro, Trio 3 Pro or ZenScreen MB16ACV themselves on a page I could open; the only measured extender figure is for an older sibling (Duex Plus, Parka Blogs).
decides: It confirms rather than overturns the picks. The Duex Max DS stays the one-cable attached pick for any Air chip, but at about 156 PPI against the Air's measured 224 PPI its text is visibly coarser. The Duex Float 2 Pro (about 189 PPI) is the closest of our screens to the Air's sharpness, so it wins the long-reading/coding segment. Its cost is power and weight: about 5.8 h instead of 16.5 h unplugged by arithmetic, brightness capped at 80% unless a 15 W or larger charger is attached, and 1.3 kg against the Air's 1.52 kg. Shoppers who work on battery should lean to the lighter Duex Max DS or plan to plug the Float in.

findings.label: Built-in display, measured maximum and average brightness
findings.source_title: Apple MacBook Air 15 M4 review: The fanless M4 SoC is years ahead of the competition (Notebookcheck, Andreas Osthoff, 2025-03-11)
findings.note: Notebookcheck measured with an X-Rite i1Pro 2; contrast 1641:1 (black level 0.32 cd/m²). This is the baseline every added screen sits next to: the extenders here are maker-rated 300–350 nits.

findings.label: Built-in display, pixel density and colour coverage
findings.note: Notebookcheck's figures. Used as the sharpness baseline for the PPI comparison below.

findings.label: Battery capacity, Wi-Fi runtime and weight
findings.value: 66.5 Wh; 16 h 28 min Wi-Fi at 150 cd/m²; 6 h 45 min at maximum brightness; 1.52 kg (3.35 lb)
findings.note: Read from the second half of the page. Notebookcheck's power figures: idle 2.2 W minimum, 11.5 W average, 11.6 W maximum; load 34.5 W average, 37.5 W maximum. Implied average draw in the Wi-Fi test: 66.5 Wh ÷ 16.47 h = 4.04 W. The review also says the M4 drives two external displays in addition to the internal panel.

findings.label: Power drawn from the MacBook on one cable, and brightness cap
findings.value: 7.5 W in Limited Power Mode, brightness capped at 80%; full brightness needs a PD USB-C charger of 15 W or more; passes up to 65 W back to the laptop
findings.source_title: Mobile Pixels Duex Float 2 Pro review: Portable screen that floats above your MacBook (Macworld, Simon Jary, 2025-12-16)
findings.note: Macworld's wording: 'The screen will draw from 7.5W of power from the MacBook in the Limited Power Mode that caps brightness at 80%.' Macworld does not say it metered this. The review does not name the test MacBook and does not mention the 15-inch Air.

findings.label: Estimated effect on MacBook Air 15 (M4) battery runtime (Dealectric arithmetic)
findings.value: about 5.8 h Wi-Fi browsing with the Float on bus power, against 16 h 28 min without it
findings.source_title: Apple MacBook Air 15 M4 review (Notebookcheck); 7.5 W from Macworld's Duex Float 2 Pro review
findings.note: Arithmetic, not a measurement: 4.04 W (Notebookcheck's implied draw) + 7.5 W (Macworld) = 11.54 W; 66.5 Wh ÷ 11.54 W = 5.76 h. Ignores USB conversion losses and the extra GPU load of a second 2560×1600 screen, so the real figure would be lower. The screen alone would use the full battery in 66.5 ÷ 7.5 = 8.9 h. Label it as an estimate if published.

findings.label: Weight and thickness against the Air's weight
findings.value: 2.9 lb (1.3 kg), 0.7 in thick unfolded; about 86% of the Air 15's 1.52 kg
findings.source_title: Mobile Pixels Duex Float 2 Pro review (Macworld, Simon Jary)
findings.note: Macworld states the weight without saying it weighed the unit. 1.3 ÷ 1.52 = 0.855 using Notebookcheck's Air weight. Macworld says the four magnets 'create a strong bond' and that the setup 'isn't as stable in use' without them. Its listed specs are 350 nits, 1200:1, 100% sRGB (72% NTSC), with no measurement method given, so treat them as Mobile Pixels' figures.

findings.label: Pixel density of the added screens against the Air 15's measured 224 PPI (Dealectric arithmetic)
findings.value: Duex Max DS 14.1 in 1920×1080: about 156 PPI; Duex Float 2 Pro 16 in 2560×1600: about 189 PPI
findings.source_title: Best Portable Monitors for Mac 2026 (Macworld) for the Float 2 Pro's size and resolution; FutureFive's Duex Max DS hands-on for the 14.1-inch 1080p panel
findings.note: PPI = √(w² + h²) ÷ diagonal: 2202.9 ÷ 14.1 = 156.2; 3018.9 ÷ 16 = 188.7. From Dealectric's own records, which I did not re-open: Trio 3 Pro 14.1 in 2240×1400 gives 187 PPI; FOPO S11 and S9G 16 in 1920×1200 give 141.5 PPI; FOPO S10 15.6 in 1080p gives 141 PPI. Macworld's roundup lists the Trio 3 Pro at 1920×1080 in its spec box but calls it QHD in the text, so re-check that against the manual. A 15.6-inch 1080p freestanding screen such as the ZenScreen MB16ACV also works out to 141 PPI; I did not open ASUS's page for it.

findings.label: Hands-on on a MacBook: added weight and hinge behaviour
findings.value: about 0.8 kg added; no hinge strain reported on an M1 MacBook Pro 14
findings.source_title: Hands-on review: Mobile Pixels Duex Max DS (FutureFive New Zealand, Owen McCarthy, 2024-02-19)
findings.note: A reviewer's observation, not an instrument measurement, and on a MacBook Pro 14, not the thinner-lidded Air. McCarthy says the rigid MacBook hinge gave a stable base and that the 300-nit panel was hard to tell from the MacBook's screen by eye; 300 nits is the maker's figure. 0.8 ÷ 1.52 = 53% of the Air 15's weight. No power draw or battery drain is given.

findings.product: Mobile Pixels Duex Plus (13.3 in, 2022 model, sibling of the Duex DS line)
findings.label: Measured brightness and sRGB coverage
findings.source_title: Review: Duex Plus portable display attachment for laptops (Parka Blogs, Teoh Yi Chie, 2022-07-12)
findings.note: Measured 'with a colour calibrator' (instrument not named) on the older Duex Plus, not the Duex Plus DS or Duex Max DS we link. Use only as a caution that no named measurement exists for the current DS screens, never as their figure. Teoh also notes the extra weight can pull the display down when the lid is tilted far back, and that it works best with the lid near vertical.

findings.source_title: Best Portable Monitors in 2026 (thisUSB); Best Portable Monitors for Mac 2026 (Macworld)
